subject: HelixAI - urgent stabilization and exec coordination for throughput & errors
messages:
From: Amir Rahman <amir@helixai.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: eng@helixai.com, procurement@helixai.com
Date: 2027-05-22T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden throughput drop & elevated 5xx — immediate help needed

Vanessa / Redwood on-call,

We started seeing a sharp drop in throughput and a spike in 5xx errors around 05:40 PDT this morning. Our production traffic to the Redwood endpoint for inference (model: rwd-omega-13b) is getting throttled by elevated error rates; p95 latency has jumped from ~220ms to 1.6s and overall throughput is down ~48%. This is impacting real customers.

We have already rotated keys and confirmed it's not a client-side regression. Logs attached (small extract) and a dashboard link below. We need exec-level coordination — our CPO is asking for an ETA to restore steady-state.

Quick facts: 
- Start: ~2027-05-22T05:40:00Z
- Affected regions: us-west-2 primary, failover to us-east-1 also impacted
- Error manifests: 502/503 and occasional model OOMs on longer sequences

Can someone from Redwood confirm receipt and propose the next steps?

Thanks,
Amir Rahman
Head of Platform, HelixAI
Attachments: helix_error_snaps_v1.zip (log extract, 2MB)
Links: https://monitoring.helixai.com/d/abcd1234/llm-latency
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Amir Rahman <amir@helixai.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop & elevated 5xx — immediate help needed

Team — acknowledged. Thanks Amir for the quick report and the logs. I'm convening an urgent stabilization sync at 09:00 PDT (30m) and inviting Ops, SRE, and Support. Goal: triage root cause, commit immediate mitigations, and prepare an executive update for Helix by 10:30 PDT.

Immediate asks for the 09:00 sync: 
- Markus: quick triage (kernel OOM vs runtime queuing vs model-serving degradation)
- Rishi: capacity view + current autoscaler behavior and any recent policy changes
- Marissa: customer comms owner and escalation path for C-suite updates
- Laura: legal/contract note on SLA credits we should pre-authorize (if required)

I will run the sync and provide a one-page status to Amir and Helix exec by 10:30 PDT. Attachments: stabilization_playbook_v0.3.pdf (draft mitigation steps).

Vanessa
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | vanessa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Amir Rahman <amir@helixai.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop & elevated 5xx — immediate help needed

09:00 sync notes (triage snapshot):
- Observed: sharp increase in token-level processing time for attention matmul on long-context requests; memory pressure on host leading to retries and 503s.
- Root candidates: recent autoscaling policy tweak (reduced max burst), and a model variant switch on a small subset of pods that changed kernel selection path.
- Short-term mitigations we can enact in the next 20–30m: 
   1) Pin affected customer traffic to the prior model variant (rwd-omega-13b-v1) with conservative sequence-length cap.
   2) Increase max_burst on the autoscaler by 25% for us-west-2 pool and force immediate scale-up of spare instances (manual hot-add).
   3) Enable temporary KV-cache reuse for repeated prefixes for Helix traffic (saves ~12–18% per-token time).
- Risks: temporary increase in unit cost; possible brief rate-limited throttles during rollout.

I will run the pinning and autoscaler override now and report back once in effect (~09:25 PDT). Logs show a correlation between the variant switch and the first spike at 05:38 PDT.

Markus
Staff Engineer — Serving Runtime
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Amir Rahman <amir@helixai.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: HelixAI stabilization update (ETA and immediate mitigations)

Amir — quick customer-facing update following our 09:00 triage: 

Summary: We identified a recent model-variant switch that altered kernel selection for longer sequences and exacerbated memory pressure under Helix's traffic profile. We've implemented three immediate mitigations:
1) Traffic pinning to rwd-omega-13b-v1 (previous kernel selection) — in progress, expected effect within 5–10 minutes.
2) Manual autoscaler override to add spare capacity in us-west-2 — done; instances coming up now.
3) Temporary KV-cache reuse for repeated prefixes on Helix routes — enabled, should reduce per-token work.

Current state (09:28 PDT): p95 latency down from 1.6s to ~600ms; throughput recovering (~82% of baseline); 5xx rate reduced by ~65%.

ETA to steady-state: 45–90 minutes. We'll continue to monitor and will provide an updated exec note by 10:30 PDT with a postmortem outline and next steps (root cause confirmation, permanent fix cadence, and optional credit/contract considerations).

If you want immediate phone coverage, I can get Markus and Rishi on a call with your engineering leadership.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: stabilization_playbook_v0.3.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Amir Rahman <amir@helixai.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: HelixAI follow-up: stabilization complete + next steps and timeline

Amir / Helix execs —

Follow-up from our morning escalation: full stabilization was reached by ~12:55 PDT after the pinned variant completed rollout and the autoscaler warmed capacity. Key outcomes: 
- p95 latency: returned to 210–260ms steady-state for typical request distributions.
- Throughput: recovered to 98% of pre-incident baseline.
- 5xx/error rate: returned to normal operating window.

Next steps and corrective plan: 
- Root cause postmortem: runtime kernel change during a staged canary caused unexpected memory amplification on long-context workloads. Engineering is preparing a postmortem; target publication: 2027-05-24 EOD.
- Permanent mitigations: improved canary gating for kernel selection, autoscaler policy guardrails, and enhanced traffic-level integration tests (target Q3).
- Credits/contract: Vanessa and Laura will align with Helix on a customer relief package; we will propose a commercial remediation by 2027-05-25.

If you'd like a joint readout for your board, we can prepare a 15–20 minute incident summary slide deck.

Thanks for working with us through this — apologies for the disruption. Please reply if you need anything else or if you want a phone handoff.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: incident-snapshot-helix-20270522.pdf (1.2MB)
